title: Everybody is on the train
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you separate work and life, or mix them, and who else lives with that choice?
A student asked about the line at the end of the chapter that vacations will kill you. Jose said: that's figurative. What I think he is saying is that a lack of focus could kill me.
He said the person is probably uncomfortable taking a vacation, because he doesn't know what a vacation is. So he asks: what am I doing here, am I taking time from the company? He is obsessive.
Do I want to go out and build an incredible company and not have a family life, and be obsessed like that? Or what is my balance? What's my risk threshold, and what's my commitment?

What is your work, play and lifestyle? he asked. Do you mix the two, or separate them like most people: this is my vacation time, this is my work time? He said he personally meshes the two: every day he is excited and having fun working, but structured.

You have to consider the people around you, he said. When his children were small his wife told him: this is a family car, you can't tell the boys to shut up because you're on a business call. You're the one imposing on their time. He said: you're right.

Our partners and kids are everybody on that train, he said. Even if you don't talk business with your wife, they will feel it and suffer it. He says: you may as well get them involved. Otherwise she doesn't know where my anxiety is coming from, and I tell my children what I'm working on and turn it into learning lessons.

He said plainly that this is his opinion and he doesn't want to sound arrogant: you have to work out what works for you. A student agreed: everyone has to work out what makes the most sense for their life.
What do the people on your train know about where you are heading?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write whether you mix work and life or separate them.
Write who pays for that choice.
Write what you will tell the people close to you about your work this week.
Write your risk threshold and your commitment.
Write one change you will make so they are not left outside.

check.q: What did Jose say about the line that vacations will kill you?
choices: It's figurative: lack of focus could kill me

check.q: What did Jose's wife tell him about the family car?
choices: You can't tell the boys to shut up because you're on a business call

check.q: What did Jose say about his own way of doing it?
choices: It is his opinion; you work out what works for you

recap: Know your balance. Remember who is on the train with you.
